title: JavaScript Jam Live Partners with React Miami: Introducing 'Miami Jam' and a Month of Web Dev Insights
outline: Introduction: Overcoming the Twitter Spaces 'Kerfuffle' and Welcoming the Community
What is JavaScript Jam Live? Meet the Hosts from Edgio
Welcome to 'React Miami Month': A Special Media Partnership
The Power of Community: Why Audience Participation Matters
Introducing 'Miami Jam': A New Interactive Game Show Format for Tech Talks
What to Expect Next: Engaging with Speakers and Audience Scoring
draft: If you have ever hosted or attended a live audio event on Twitter Spaces, you know that technical hiccups are practically a rite of passage. Even for seasoned technology professionals, there is always a new quirk waiting to test your patience. During a recent episode of JavaScript Jam Live, the hosts experienced a classic Twitter Space 'kerfuffle' where the room appeared to be starting on the host's phone without actually going live for the public. As developer advocate Anthony Campolo noted, the secret to solving this particular glitch is simply patience—waiting one to two minutes usually allows the platform to sort itself out. Once the digital dust settled, the team kicked off a massive announcement: an exciting new media partnership with the upcoming React Miami conference. What is JavaScript Jam Live? For those who might be new to the format, JavaScript Jam Live is an open-mic style audio event dedicated to all things JavaScript and web development. Hosted by the team at Edgio, an edge deployment platform, the show thrives on casual, insightful conversations and heavy audience participation. The regular hosting lineup includes Ishan Anand, VP of Product at Edgio; Anthony Campolo, Developer Advocate at Edgio; and Scott Steinlage, Technical Community Manager at Edgio. Together, they facilitate a welcoming space where developers from all walks of life can share news, debate opinions, and discuss the latest trends in the web ecosystem. Welcome to React Miami Month. While the episode was initially promoted as a special week of programming, Scott Steinlage quickly officially renamed the initiative to 'React Miami Month.' Through an official media partnership with the React Miami conference, JavaScript Jam Live is expanding its programming to bring listeners closer to the event's speakers, organizers, and core topics. Despite the influx of high-profile conference guests, the hosts emphasized that the traditional, laid-back JavaScript Jam vibe will remain intact. The partnership is simply designed to inject even more value into the weekly sessions. Over the coming weeks, various speakers from the React Miami lineup will join the stage to discuss the specific topics that matter to them, offering listeners a preview of the conference's overarching themes. The Power of Community Participation. A core pillar of the JavaScript Jam philosophy is inclusivity. During the broadcast, Scott made a point to remind listeners that the stage is open to everyone, regardless of whether they are a complete beginner writing their first lines of code or an advanced engineer who has been in the industry for decades. When audience members request the mic to ask questions, offer comments, or share facts and opinions, it elevates the value of the conversation for everyone listening in. This collaborative spirit was on full display as community members, along with React Miami organizer Michelle, hopped on stage to celebrate the partnership. Michelle noted that the conference organizers decided to give the media partners—Scott, Anthony, and fellow partner Dev Agrawal—the green light to be completely creative with their pre-conference programming. Introducing 'Miami Jam': A Tech Game Show. With the freedom to experiment, Dev Agrawal (who also goes by Dave) revealed a brand-new event concept developed in collaboration with Anthony and Scott. Taking place the following week, the trio will host an interactive show called 'Miami Jam.' Traditionally, pre-conference media coverage relies heavily on standard interview or panel formats, where hosts bring speakers on stage and ask predictable questions about their talk abstracts and personal motivations. Miami Jam aims to flip this script entirely by turning the speaker showcase into a lively game show. Instead of straightforward interview prompts, the hosts will challenge React Miami speakers with trivia-style questions. These prompts will cover a wide range of entertaining and educational subjects, including React-specific trivia, weird quirks found in JavaScript and TypeScript, and 'guess the library' challenges. In an effort to cross-pollinate ideas, speakers might even be asked questions directly related to another speaker's conference topic. Bridging Fun and Deep Technical Insights. While the trivia format guarantees a fun and lighthearted atmosphere, the ultimate goal of Miami Jam is still to extract deep, meaningful insights from the guests. The game show mechanics are designed to act as a natural segue into more detailed, in-depth technical discussions. After a trivia question is answered, the hosts will use the topic as a springboard to explore the speaker's upcoming React Miami presentation, their personal journey in the tech industry, and the real-world projects they have worked on that inspired their talk. This structure fosters a much more collaborative environment, encouraging speakers to share experiences with one another rather than speaking in isolated silos. Getting the Audience Involved. True to the ethos of JavaScript Jam Live, Miami Jam will not treat the audience as passive listeners. Dev explained that attendees will play an active role in how the game unfolds. Beyond simply asking questions to the speakers on stage, audience members will actually help dictate the scoreboard. When an audience member poses a question to a speaker, or when the hosts throw out a particularly tough trivia prompt, the audience will have the power to decide how many points the speaker receives for their answer. By blending gamification with technical education, the React Miami media partners are setting the stage for an unforgettable month of community-driven web development content.
